{{Short description|French physicist}}
'''Bernard Sadoulet''' (born 23 April 1944 in [[Nice]])<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale, 2004</ref> is a French physicist.

Sadoulet studied from 1963 to 1965 at the [[École polytechnique]] and received his doctorate in 1971 at [[University of Paris-Sud]] in [[Orsay]]. From 1966 to 1973, he worked at [[CERN]] and from 1976 at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. He was involved in the design of the [[UA1 experiment|UA1 detector]] at CERN.<ref name=Homepage>{{cite web|title=Bernard Sadoulet|website=Physics @ Berkeley|url=https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/bernard-sadoulet}}</ref>

In the 1990s and 2000s, he was engaged in the search for [[dark matter]] in the form of [[WIMPs]]. He developed cryogenic detectors to discover these WIMPs through the [[phonon]]s they generated by collisions in crystals. Specifically, he initiated the [[Cryogenic Dark Matter Search]] (CDMS) experiments at the [[Soudan Underground Laboratory]] in Minnesota with [[Blas Cabrera Navarro]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cdms.berkeley.edu/Education/DMpages/science/detectors.shtml |title=CDMS II Detector |access-date=2019-04-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111126184537/http://cdms.berkeley.edu/Education/DMpages/science/detectors.shtml |archive-date=2011-11-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://physics.aps.org/articles/v2/2 Karl van Bibber, APS, about SuperCDMS, 2009]</ref>

In 2013 he received the [[Panofsky Prize]] with Blas Cabrera.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Sadoulet&first_nm=Bernard&year=2013|title=2013 W.K.H. Panofsky Prize in Experimental Particle Physics Recipient, Bernard Sadoulet|website=American Physical Society}}</ref> Sadoulet is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1991&unit_id=DAP&institution=}} (search on year=1991 and nominating unit=DAP)</ref> the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and the American Association for the Advancement of Science. In 2012, he was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. Since 1985, he has been a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. From 1989 to 2001, he was director of the Center for Particle Astrophysics. He is currently the director of the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|LBNL]] Institute for Nuclear and Particle Astrophysics and Cosmology (INPA).<ref name=Homepage/><ref>{{cite web|website=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, lbl.gov|title=The Institute for Nuclear and Particle Astrophysics|url=https://inpa.lbl.gov}}</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Vuk Mandic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bernard Sadoulet|website=Physics Tree|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=127963}}</ref>
